Off the Books: Perks 0.4.0

WHAT IT DOES
It adds 29 starting perks to the new-game screen: trading, customers, appraisal,
security, scavenging and nights out. Some cost points, some give points back as
drawbacks. A perk works only in a run that was started with it. The mod needs no other
mod.

HOW TO USE IT
Pick perks when you start a run, as you pick the game's own. Each perk has its own icon.
The run summary, shown after buying the shop or at the end of a run, shows the starting
perks in rows of eight.
"Ordinary" below means the everyday customers and suppliers who come back: not security,
not wanted persons, not story characters and not customers an event sends.

THE PERKS
Jack of All Trades and Head Start are for a free-build run. They throw the balance of
everything else, and are meant to.

Master Valuer (costs 2 points)
Appraisals pay you 25% more.
Counted on what the appraisal paid you.

Appraisal Advert (costs 1 point)
With a certificate in the showcase, each day has a 25% chance of an extra appraisal customer.
The customer still waits out the game's usual pause between visits.

Cooling-Off Deal (costs 1 point)
Stolen goods you buy arrive 15% cooler.
Once per item, when you buy it.

Lights-Out Premium (costs 1 point)
Customers pay 15% more during a blackout.
Ordinary customers only.

Private Viewing (costs 2 points)
A luxury buyer visits once a week with twice the usual budget, and pays 10% under your price.
The usual budget is the average of that day's ordinary customers who have one. The day is picked afresh each week.

Trusted Wholesaler (costs 2 points)
Suppliers charge 10% less. Rules out Greedy Wholesaler.
Ordinary suppliers only.

Good Name (costs 1 point)
Trades earn 15% more reputation.
Gains from trades with ordinary customers. Losses stay as they are.

Hard Bargainer (costs 2 points)
Asking for 10% or less always works, unless the customer never haggles.
Any bargain of 10% or less that had a chance goes through.

Night Owl (costs 3 points)
Three outings a night, and no lost customer the morning after.
The game normally sends one customer fewer after a night out.

Window Dresser (costs 2 points)
A stocked showcase makes the shop 50 more attractive.
Added after Shabby Front, if you have both.

Thorough Search (costs 2 points)
Each find at the Dumping Grounds has a 25% chance of a second item.
The second item comes from the same loot and brings no extra risk of a wound.

Friend on the Force (costs 3 points)
Routine inspections come half as often.
The wait between inspections is doubled. With Marked Shop as well, it ends up one and a half times as long.

Wealthy Visitors (costs 3 points)
Everyone who comes in has 25% more to spend.
Every visitor with a budget, story characters included.

Brisk Trade (costs 3 points)
Your first three sales each day pay 10% extra, up to 25 each.
Sales to ordinary buyers. The extra is paid to you on top and does not come out of the customer's budget. Several items sold in one go count as one sale.

Jack of All Trades (costs 3 points)
Free build: room for 12 more perks.
For a run where you want to pick freely.

Head Start (gives 12 points)
Free build: 12 extra perk points.
For a run where you want to pick freely. Goes well with Jack of All Trades.

Tech Dealer (costs 1 point)
Machines, modules and nodes sell for 15% more. Everything else sells for 10% less. Not for filled containers. Rules out Bargain Bin and Bulky Goods.
Sales to ordinary buyers. A container with something in it sells at its usual price.

Bargain Bin (costs 1 point)
Goods worth 50 or less sell for 15% more. Goods worth 200 or more sell for 10% less. Not for filled containers. Rules out Tech Dealer and Bulky Goods.
Sales to ordinary buyers, by the value of one unit. A container with something in it sells at its usual price.

Bulky Goods (costs 1 point)
Goods of 6 squares or more sell for 15% more. Goods of 2 squares or fewer sell for 10% less. Not for filled containers. Rules out Tech Dealer and Bargain Bin.
Sales to ordinary buyers. Squares are the item's width times its height. A container with something in it sells at its usual price.

Premium Retailer (free)
You sell for 5% more, and suppliers charge you 10% more.
Ordinary buyers and ordinary suppliers.

Marked Shop (gives 2 points)
Stolen goods come 25% hotter, and inspections come 25% sooner.
The heat is raised when an item first becomes stolen goods. The wait between inspections is a quarter shorter.

Shabby Front (gives 2 points)
The shop is 150 less attractive, and renovations cost 25% more.
Attractiveness never goes below zero.

Tight Regulars (gives 1 point)
Returning customers have 15% less to spend.
Ordinary customers who have been in before.

Careless Digger (gives 1 point)
Wounds at the Dumping Grounds are 5 points more likely. Rules out Careful Scavenger.
Both the minor and the major wound chance.

Aug Bounty (gives 2 points)
One Aug in four brings a second.
On a day an Aug is due, there is a 25% chance that another comes the same day. Never more than two.

Steep Overheads (gives 1 point)
Power, cleaning, insurance and referrals cost 25% more.
The extra is taken each night after the services are paid, and shows as a line in the morning report.

Lean Suppliers (gives 2 points)
Suppliers bring a quarter less.
Every fourth item an ordinary supplier would have offered is left out.

Skimmed Till (gives 1 point)
5% of every sale goes missing, at most 10 a day.
Sales to ordinary buyers. Several items sold in one go count as one sale.

Greedy Wholesaler (gives 2 points)
Suppliers charge 10% more. Rules out Trusted Wholesaler.
Ordinary suppliers only.

SETTINGS
All are in Options, under Off the Books: Perks, and in the Mods list. All start on.
Restart the game after a change.
- Enable Perks: switches the effects of all perks.
- Offer <perk name> in a new game: one switch per perk. Off keeps the perk off the
  new-game screen. A run that already has the perk keeps its effect, and after such a
  run is loaded the perk shows on the new-game screen again until you restart.
A perk that cannot work with your game version is left off the new-game screen. After a
saved run that had such a perk is loaded, the perk can still show there, at no cost and
without effect, until you restart.

WHAT IT CHANGES
The perks change prices, budgets, reputation, how often customers and inspections
come, appraisal pay, scavenging finds and your cash, as each perk says above. The mod
saves two small notes in the save's mod data: the last day the Appraisal Advert was
rolled for and the last day a Private Viewing visit was queued.

BEFORE YOU REMOVE THIS MOD
Switch Off the Books: Perks off in the Mods menu and restart, or delete its folder while
the game is closed. A run that had these perks still lists them, and they no longer do
anything.

WITH OTHER MODS
If another mod offers a perk that does the same job as one of these, pick one of the
two: with both, the effects add up.

WHEN SOMETHING SEEMS WRONG
Player.log has a line starting with [Perks] that says how many perks were registered
and how many are not working. If one is not working, another [Perks] line says why.

TRANSLATIONS
Translations are very welcome: every text is in Localization/en.csv. Send a translated
copy on GitHub: https://github.com/rnk-gaming/probably-stolen-mods/issues
